data.field_of_study: International Affairs; Public Policy; Public Service

data.evidence_sentence: This gives well qualified young people with a strong interest in politics from the USA, France, Israel and Central, Eastern and South Eastern Europe and Arab region the opportunity to gain first-hand experience of Germany's system of parliamentary government.
data.notes: Name mismatch: the page describes the International Parliamentary Scholarship (IPS) for Germany, not a general German Bundestag Scholarship. The page lists a 13-week work placement with a Member of the Bundestag, not degree study, so degree level is other. Eligibility lists 'Citizenship of participant country' but the page names USA, France, Israel and regions without a full country list, so the nationality rule is a best reading. Page also lists fourth-year+ undergrads and undergraduate alumni as eligible applicants, which conflicts with the 'University degree' criterion. Deadline 'July' has no year and is past, so annual:07. Benefits: 500 euros per month, free accommodation, insurance and travel expenses. Enrollment status 'applicant' is inferred from the application process. Points to bundestag.de/ips for details. Page includes ASU-internal citizenship status and nomination fields (no nomination required).
